appearance_facts.fact: Chart title is 'Monthly Water Pumping Volume'.
Y-axis is labeled 'Pumping volume (m3)' with a scale from 10,000 to 40,000 in increments of 5,000.
X-axis is labeled 'Month' and displays the months: Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar, May.
The bar for May is the shortest, visually representing a pumping volume near 10,000 m3.
The bar for Jan is the tallest, visually representing a pumping volume of 40,000 m3.
The bar for Apr is visually high, representing a pumping volume of 30,000 m3.
The bar for Mar is visually medium-high, representing a pumping volume of 27,000 m3.
The bar for Feb is visually medium, representing a pumping volume of 20,000 m3.

printed_facts.fact: Months are labeled from left to right as: Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar, May.
The bar for May is visually at or just above the 10,000 m3 level.
The bar for Jan reaches the 40,000 m3 level.
The bar for Apr reaches the 30,000 m3 level.
The bar for Mar reaches the 27,000 m3 level.
The bar for Feb reaches the 20,000 m3 level.
The bar for Jun is visually at or just above the 17,000 m3 level.

public_definitions: The goal is to review the monthly water pumping dashboard and decide whether May should be handled as a standard low-pumping follow-up or escalated as a critical low-pumping anomaly for this reporting cycle.
The chart is titled 'Monthly Water Pumping Volume'.
The primary field label is 'May low-pumping route'.
The options are: 'Route May to standard low-pumping follow-up', 'Escalate May to critical low-pumping anomaly review', 'Send May to background monthly record filing'.
The companion fields include 'note', 'Program area', 'Review scope', 'Record workflow', and 'Routing criterion'.
The page instructions direct the user to use the dashboard to determine the appropriate low-pumping severity route for May.
